reports.title: HawkEye 360 Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Full Year 2026 Outlook
section: For full-year 2026, the Company is increasing its total revenue expectations to $225 million and $227 million, and non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of between $38 million and $40 million.

desk.headline: Revenue up 84% to $59.3m, above estimates; full-year revenue and EBITDA outlook raised
results: Revenue rose 84% to $59.3m, helped by the ISA acquisition; international sales rose 76% to a record $23.3m.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to $13.3m from $9.6m, but higher costs and depreciation left a small net loss of $0.2m.
Operating cash flow was $9.6m; after $9.5m of satellite and equipment spending, free cash flow was about break-even.
Backlog reached $300.3m, and a further $135m of contracts were signed after the quarter, over $70m of them in Europe.
After its IPO the company holds $494.9m in cash and has repaid its term loans.

guidance.summary: HawkEye 360 lifted its 2026 revenue range to $225–227m (from $215–220m) and its adjusted EBITDA range to $38–40m (from $30–36m).

points: Management said international sales are nearing half the business, spread over more than 40 countries and agencies.
The $135m of post-quarter contracts were said to give the company what it needs to hit its 2026 revenue target.
US government work grew about 25% from Q2, including a first operational contract with the NRO; budget delays remain a risk.
The CFO warned Q3 margins are not a steady run rate, as Q4 includes extra spending on capacity.
Plans for 2027 include the first new-generation Kestrel satellite launch in Q1 and selective small acquisitions.
call.source: HawkEye 360 (HAWK) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — The Motley Fool, 13 Nov 2026

watch: Q4 delivery against the raised $225–227m revenue range.
US budget timing, including any continuing resolution, and export-licence delays on overseas deals.
Commissioning of Clusters 15 and 16 and the 2027 satellite launches.
